content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT: LoRA, QLoRA, Prefix Tuning)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As Large Language Models (LLMs) scale to billions of parameters, full fine-tuning becomes computationally prohibitive. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) addresses this challenge by updating only a small subset of parameters while freezing the pre-trained base model. This tutorial covers the mechanics, implementation details, and trade-offs of the most prominent PEFT methodologies: LoRA, QLoRA, and Prefix Tuning."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Understanding Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"LoRA hypothesizes that the weight updates during fine-tuning lie in a lower intrinsic rank. Instead of updating the full weight matrix W of dimension d x k, LoRA injects trainable rank decomposition matrices. The forward pass is modified such that h = Wx + BAx, where B is of dimension d x r, A is of dimension r x k, and the rank r << min(d, k)."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class LoRALayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, rank=4, alpha=16):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_features, in_features))
        self.weight.requires_grad = False
        
        self.lora_A = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(rank, in_features))
        self.lora_B = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_features, rank))
        self.scaling = alpha / rank
        
    def forward(self, x):
        base_out = torch.matmul(x, self.weight.t())
        lora_out = torch.matmul(torch.matmul(x, self.lora_A.t()), self.lora_B.t())
        return base_out + (lora_out * self.scaling)"},{"order":6,"type":"heading","text":"2. Quantized LoRA (QLoRA)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"QLoRA pushes efficiency further by quantizing the pre-trained base model to 4-bit precision using NormalFloat4 (NF4) data types and introducing double quantization to save additional memory. It freezes the 4-bit base model and attaches trainable 16-bit LoRA adapters, making it feasible to fine-tune models like LLaMA-65B on a single consumer GPU."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"4-bit NormalFloat (NF4): An information-theoretically optimal quantization datatype for normally distributed weights."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Double Quantization: Quantizes the quantization constants themselves to reduce memory footprint further."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Paged Optimizers: Uses CUDA unified memory to manage memory spikes and prevent out-of-memory errors during gradient accumulation."},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"3. Prefix Tuning"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Prefix Tuning is an additive PEFT method that prepends a trainable continuous prompt (a sequence of continuous task-specific vectors) to the keys and values of the attention mechanism at every layer. Unlike discrete prompt tuning, these prefix activations are optimized directly via gradient descent."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Conceptual illustration of prefix injection in multi-head attention
import torch

def inject_prefix(key_states, value_states, prefix_k, prefix_v):
    # prefix_k, prefix_v shape: (batch_size, num_heads, prefix_len, head_dim)
    k_prime = torch.cat([prefix_k, key_states], dim=2)
    v_prime = torch.cat([prefix_v, value_states], dim=2)
    return k_prime, v_prime"},{"order":14,"type":"heading","text":"Summary and Comparison"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LoRA: Best general-purpose PEFT method; preserves inference latency by merging adapter weights into the base model."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"QLoRA: Ideal for hardware-constrained environments where base model memory footprint must be minimized through 4-bit quantization."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prefix Tuning: Highly effective for generation tasks, though it slightly reduces the available sequence context length due to prepended tokens."}]
